---
title: "Stage 0b — restructure, then regenerate"
---

Moving the misplaced elements into the M11 structure, and then making something read the result.

**This stage exists only on the retrofit path.** If the protocol was authored to M11 there is
nothing to restructure, and you go straight from confirmation to generating the study
definition. Everything below is about closing a gap that a protocol authored to the template
never opens.

## What this is

Stage 0 found the estimands in the SAP rather than the protocol. Stage 0b moves them, section
by section, and regenerates the downstream artefact from the restructured protocol instead of
from the original prose.

## What you do

Move the sections. Then re-run the generator so the USDM fragment is a *product* of the M11
protocol rather than a transcription of the original.

## What you should see

A restructured protocol, and a regenerated fragment that is visibly richer than the
hand-authored one — because the structure now supplies what prose had left implicit.

## What to look out for

**Done means both halves.** A restructured section that nothing consumes leaves the next
stage still transcribing from prose, and looks like progress while changing nothing.

The payoff is concrete and worth expecting: regenerating took this study's fragment from one
estimand to six, because M11 §3 supplies what the SAP had been holding.
